CLARIFICATION OF THE OPERATOR'S DESIGN (b) — the Orchestrator explained it back wrongly and the correct version is cheaper than either variant in your brief. They then identified the real constraint themselves: they want Bellman/memoisation so forward nodes can be RECYCLED across different bracketed roots and across branches of the same search. That recycling is what forces the design, and here is the resolution: the capture counter belongs in the SEARCH MEMO KEY, not in the persistent table key. A node reached from root P1 with c=3 is a genuinely different memo entry from the same position reached from P2 with c=1, so the memo key is (colex, side, ko, passes, c) — but the persistent WZO2 table keeps its existing key and never grows.
